$schema-note: Exemptions from the Baseline floor enforced by scripts/check-baseline.mjs.
The floor is 'newly' (Baseline Newly available). A feature below the floor
may be used unguarded only via an entry here, and only when failing to
support it is INERT -- the browser drops the declaration and the result is
still correct. Features where absence changes layout or correctness belong
in an @supports guard instead, not in this file.
Every entry needs 'reason', 'degradation' and 'reviewBy'. The checker fails
the build when an entry is unused, when its feature has since reached the
floor, or when 'reviewBy' has passed -- a stale exemption is a silent lie
about the support policy, so it breaks the build like any other violation.

allow.degradation: Checkbox and radio controls render in the UA default accent colour instead of --ui-color-primary. Purely cosmetic; no layout or behaviour change.
allow.reason: BCD data gap, not a real support gap. The support record lists chrome 93, edge 93, firefox 92, firefox_android 92, safari 26.2 and safari_ios 26.2, but has no chrome_android entry at all, and Baseline requires all seven. The property shipped in Chrome 93 across platforms. Re-check once BCD backfills the record.

allow.degradation: On Safari, an open .ui-drawer whose content is too short to scroll chains its scroll to the page behind it. Cosmetic -- the drawer still traps focus, light-dismisses, and returns focus to the burger.
allow.reason: Neither a data gap nor something @supports can cover. Every engine shipped this partial_implementation -- it has no effect on scroll containers without scrollable overflow. Chrome fixed that in 144 and Firefox in 150; Safari has not (webkit.org/b/243452), so Baseline counts it unsupported. Crucially Safari still PARSES the property, so `@supports (overscroll-behavior: contain)` evaluates true there: a guard would protect nothing while appearing to. A partial implementation therefore always belongs here rather than behind a guard.
